1) Ben: add conservative vs aggressive commit stitching options (monthly -> quarterly cadence) with the price impact and burst lane mechanics.
2) Kim/Laura: include SLA credit schedule permutations — one that preserves current uptime SLO and a second that uses a stepped-credit model for the first two quarters.

Sarah, attaching a short QBR PDF and a spreadsheet with proposed SLA options. If useful, Ben can walk the procurement team through the mechanics.

Sarah / team — attaching my recommended stitch options. TL;DR:
- Conservative stitch (recommended if HeliumTech prioritizes predictability): keep effective committed units steady at monthly equivalent but bill quarterly; includes a 5% price uplift for quarterly liquidity. Burst lane unchanged (30% burst above commit, subject to throttling at sustained >72 hours).
- Aggressive stitch (recommended if HeliumTech wants unit cost reduction): 10% increase in committed tokens vs current run-rate, 6% discount to per-token price, with a smaller burst lane (20%) and an operational credit holdback for the first 60 days.

Estimated 12-month dollar impact: Conservative = +$42k vs current MRR; Aggressive = -$28k vs current MRR but requires commit increase and usage smoothing. I put scenario math in the spreadsheet column "Stitch_Scenarios".

Also calling out an ops ask: to hit the aggressive plan's econ, HeliumTech should enable prefix caching for their high-traffic prompt families — that reduces token issuance on the order of 10–18% depending on cache hit rate. We can run a 2-week pilot before the renewal to validate.

Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_sla_options_v2.xlsx (updated with Stitch_Scenarios tab)
